prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Alo Yoga (company_id alo-yoga; category: yoga apparel and athleisure)
Official domains: aloyoga.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://amworldgroup.com/blog/alo-yoga | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"These stories create emotional connections between the brand and its audience while providing social proof that reinforces Alo's positioning within the wellness community. The authentic nature of these stories resonates strongly with target customers who value genuine experiences over polished marketing messages. Seasonal content campaigns align product launches with lifestyle moments and wellness trends, creating natural opportunities for product integration within valuable content."

[P2] source: https://www.latterly.org/alo-yoga-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2007, 2024 | published: unknown
"Alo Yoga Marketing Strategy: Through Social Commerce and Influencer Partnerships Alo Yoga emerged in 2007 with a clear vision for elevated activewear and mindful movement, then converted culture into commerce at scale. The brand built a thriving ecosystem that spans apparel, wellness content, and experiential retail, anchored in premium positioning and relentless storytelling. Estimated 2024 revenue ranges from 1.2 to 1.4 billion dollars, reflecting strong global demand and efficient digital acquisition. Marketing serves as the growth engine, moving audiences from aspiration to purchase through social commerce, ambassadors, and community experiences."

[P3] source: https://www.latterly.org/alo-yoga-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Core Elements of the Alo Yoga Marketing Strategy In a crowded athleisure market, differentiation depends on brand meaning, channel strength, and product momentum. Alo Yoga focuses on premium positioning, content-fueled demand, and experiential retail to stand apart. The strategy links aspiration and access, then sustains loyalty through subscriptions, classes, and events that extend the brand lifestyle. * Premium-first identity: Elevated design, influencer credibility, and wellness culture set higher perceived value and pricing power. * Social commerce engine: Shoppable Instagram, TikTok Shop, and creator storefronts reduce friction from discovery to checkout."

[P4] source: https://amworldgroup.com/blog/alo-yoga | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The #AloYoga hashtag has generated over 8 million posts across various social platforms, creating a vast library of authentic brand content that showcases products in real-world contexts. This user-generated content spans from yoga studio sessions to street style photography, demonstrating the versatility that supports Alo's \"studio-to-street\" positioning. The diversity of content also shows how the brand appeals to different segments within their target audience while maintaining consistent brand aesthetics. Alo actively encourages user-generated content through strategic campaigns, product launches, and community challenges that motivate customers to share their experiences."

[P5] source: https://amworldgroup.com/blog/alo-yoga | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"High-profile partnerships with fitness influencers and wellness practitioners provide credibility within the core yoga and fitness communities while extending reach to broader lifestyle audiences. These collaborations often involve co-created content, limited edition product lines, and shared experiences that provide mutual value for both the brand and the partner. The resulting content feels organic and engaging rather than overtly promotional, which is essential for maintaining authenticity with Alo's sophisticated target audience. The ambassador program extends beyond celebrities to include grassroots practitioners, local studio owners, and emerging fitness personalities."

[P6] source: https://www.latterly.org/alo-yoga-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Campaign visuals pair clean, modern design with tactile fabric close-ups, which reinforce quality and fit. Alo highlights real instructors and creators alongside celebrities, creating a spectrum of aspiration and authenticity. The balance drives trust, while consistent color grading, typography, and spatial composition create recognizable creative coherence across channels. The narrative expands across always-on content, seasonal launches, and experiential moments. To guide execution, Alo organizes content around pillars that translate easily across social, retail, and events. These pillars fuel measurable engagement and keep the brand message focused as product lines broaden."

[P7] source: https://www.opensend.com/post/alo-yoga-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Technical specifications matter, but they rarely create lasting competitive advantages. Experience, community, and brand positioning create stronger differentiation. The retail environment itself becomes a marketing asset. Alo's stores are designed to be photographed, with lighting and staging that flatter both products and customers. This user-generated content then flows to social media, creating organic marketing that reinforces brand positioning. The physical space becomes a content studio that generates marketing assets continuously."

[P8] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/alo-yoga-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Alo Yoga’s Social Media Marketing Strategy Alo Yoga knows how vital social media is for its brand. It uses platforms like Instagram to build a strong community. Through Instagram, Alo Yoga shares its message and connects with people. Alo Yoga works with yoga influencers to grow its brand in the yoga world. These partnerships make the brand more trusted and real. By choosing influencers wisely, Alo makes sure they fit with the brand’s look and values. The Pro Program by Alo Yoga helps establish the brand as a yoga authority. It offers discounts to yoga instructors who then promote Alo Yoga’s products. This builds a group of loyal fans and marks Alo Yoga as a leader in yoga gear."

[P9] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/alo-yoga-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Besides Instagram, Alo has a big presence on YouTube. It posts videos and live streams about yoga and wellness. This content shows Alo Yoga’s dedication to the yoga community, boosting its brand identity online. Alo Yoga encourages its customers to tell friends about the brand through a referral program. This makes customers more loyal and spreads the word about Alo Yoga. Earned media is key to Alo Yoga’s marketing. The brand gets celebrities and customers to talk about it on TikTok and Instagram. This creates natural excitement and conversation around Alo Yoga. Alo Yoga’s efforts online link the brand with a healthy lifestyle."

[P10] source: https://www.modash.io/breakdowns/alo-yoga-influencer-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics, creator_or_influencer_audience_data | dates in text: none | published: unknown
